entities.summary: The Euthydikos Kore is a late Archaic, Parian marble statue of the kore type, dated to c. 490–480 BCE, that once stood amongst the votive sculptures on the Acropolis of Athens. It was destroyed during the Persian invasion of 480 BCE and found in the Perserschutt. It is named after the dedication on the base of the sculpture, "Euthydikos son of Thaliarchos dedicated [me]". It now stands in the Acropolis Museum.
